subject.title: Follow-up: optimize fallback order + add model-input config guardrail

question: Should this issue remain the broad tracker for benchmark-backed fallback ordering while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/50287 owns model-input guardrails, or should maintainers replace it with a narrower fallback-policy item?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but fallback ranking requires live benchmark/product policy and the guardrail half can affect the public configured-model capability contract, so automation should not choose the permanent policy and tracking shape alone.

options.title: Keep As Fallback Policy Tracker
options.body: Keep this issue open for the benchmark-backed fallback ordering decision and let the focused guardrail issue own schema/capability validation.

options.title: Replace With Narrow Fallback Tracker
options.body: Create or identify one narrower fallback optimization issue, then close this broad follow-up once both halves have canonical homes.

options.title: Defer Fallback Policy Work
options.body: Leave explicit configured fallback order as the supported behavior for now and document why benchmark-ranked fallback policy is not planned in this cycle.

recommendation.title: Keep As Fallback Policy Tracker
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for the benchmark-backed fallback ordering decision and let the focused guardrail issue own schema/capability validation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from the issue timeline and fallback/provider-routing history.
